We are looking for a Principal Solutions Architect to design how networks become quantum-safe — for the largest network operators, enterprises, and government agencies in the world.

Today's networks are secured with cryptography that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer will break. Every operator and enterprise will have to inventory their cryptography, make it agile, migrate to post-quantum algorithms, and in the highest-assurance segments complement that with quantum-safe key distribution. Almost nobody knows yet what that architecture actually looks like. That is the problem you will solve — first with customers, on real networks, and then as reusable architectures that shape what IonQ builds.

This role sits deliberately in two places. About half your time is customer-facing: in collaboration with our GTM colleagues, you’ll be leading architecture discussions, designing quantum-safe target architectures and migration paths, running proofs of concept and interoperability tests, and supporting complex pursuits as the technical authority. The other half is design authority, standards work, and providing thought leadership internally and externally: turning what you learn in the field into reference architectures, migration playbooks, standards, whitepapers, blogs, and product requirements that our engineering and product teams build against.

You are equally comfortable in a firewall design review as you are in a discussion about hybrid key exchange and crypto-agility. You can explain to a CISO why their crypto inventory is the hard part, and to a network engineer exactly which IPsec algorithms to use and where they could insert external key material in order to become quantum-safe.

This is not a software architecture role — you will not own a codebase (it’s a plus if you can do some scripting). It is an architecture and customer role: you own designs, decisions, and the technical credibility of IonQ's quantum-safe networking story.

Responsibilities:

  • Design quantum-safe target architectures and migration paths for customer networks — spanning WAN and transport, data center and campus, segmentation and access control, key management, and the crypto that underpins all of it.
  • Lead technical discovery and architecture workshops with network, security, and infrastructure teams. Assess the current state, identify where cryptography is embedded and where it is brittle, and build a migration plan the customer can actually execute.
  • Own the technical thread in complex pursuits: architecture proposals, RFI/RFP responses, security and compliance questions, competitive positioning, and objection handling — in partnership with Sales.
  • In collaboration with the Sales Engineers, design and run proofs of concept, interoperability tests, and pilots — including PQC and hybrid key exchange in production-representative network environments and, where relevant, QKD-integrated links — together with our engineering teams and customer staff.
  • Translate field learning into reusable reference architectures, migration playbooks, interoperability matrices, and design guides that scale beyond the deals you personally work.
  • Serve as the customer's voice in the product process. Bring architectural constraints, integration gaps, and roadmap requirements to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to be actionable, and hold us to them.
  • Track how the standards and threat landscape actually move and contribute to them — NIST PQC standards and migration guidance, protocol work in the IETF, national and sector-specific mandates and deadlines — and keep our architectures and guidance ahead of it.
  • Partner with Marketing, Corporate Communications, and GTM to build IonQ's technical presence in the networking and security community: talks, papers, blogs, standards bodies, and industry events.
  • Raise the technical bar around you — architecture reviews, mentoring, and the design patterns the rest of the team reuses.

Requirements:

  • 15+ years designing and securing enterprise and/or service provider networks, in a solutions architecture, network architecture, security architecture, or senior customer-facing engineering capacity.
  • Deep (hands-on) knowledge of how networks are built and secured today: routing and switching, IP transport, network segmentation, firewall and access control design, VPN and encryption at the network layer, and Zero Trust principles applied to real infrastructure. Multi-vendor experience (for example, Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Nokia) is expected.
  • Working knowledge of applied cryptography as it appears in networks: TLS, IPsec, MACsec, PKI and certificate lifecycle, key management, and how algorithm and key material choices are made and changed in practice.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in front of customers at multiple levels — leading workshops, running architecture discussions with engineers, and holding a credible conversation with a CISO or SVP of Infrastructure about risk, cost, and sequencing.
  • A serious interest in where this is heading, and enough grounding to be credible on day one: post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility, quantum key distribution, and the migration challenge facing existing networks. You do not need to have shipped a PQC migration — very few people have — but you should be able to reason about the problem rigorously and be visibly motivated to go deep.
  • Strong written communication. Architectures, migration plans, and design guidance are a large part of the output.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Willingness to travel up to 30%, primarily within the US, with incidental international travel.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with post-quantum cryptography migration: cryptographic discovery and inventory, crypto-agility architecture, hybrid key exchange, or PQC deployment in a network or PKI context.
  • Hands-on exposure to quantum key distribution or quantum networking — testbeds, carrier or research trials, key delivery interfaces to encryptors, or optical and transport-layer integration.
  • Experience at a network or security vendor, service provider, hyperscaler, or a large enterprise network or security team — with real accountability for architecture decisions at scale.
  • Familiarity with the security and compliance frameworks customers will map this work to: NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, ISO 27001, FISMA, FedRAMP, or sector-specific regulation.
  • Public-sector, defense, financial services, or telecom experience, where high-assurance and long data-confidentiality horizons make this problem urgent today.
  • Contributions to standards or the technical community: IETF, ETSI, national PQC migration working groups, published writing, or conference talks.
  • Certifications that validate technical depth — CISSP, CCIE/JNCIE, CCNP Security, or equivalent.
  • Comfort with automation and tooling — Python, config-as-code, network telemetry — enough to build a credible demo or analysis yourself rather than waiting on someone else.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Head of Finance

Cluster: Finance

Salary: USD 87,845.85 Per Annum, (Excluding Benefits)

Contract Type: Permanent, subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability

Location: Remote (the successful candidate must have the right to work in the location where they are based)

Reports to: Chief Operations Officer

Direct Reports: Finance Manager (7 Indirect Finance Staff)

Role Overview:

The Head of Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for CIVICUS’ financial management. The role combines strategic thinking and hands on delivery and requires a leader who can thrive in a dynamic mission driven and solutions focussed environment with high levels of accountability and transparency. Focussed environment with high levels of accountability and transparency.

The Head of Finance is responsible for managing CIVICUS’s finance team, organisational financial strategy, budgeting and planning, financial reporting, audit management, risk oversight and compliance with funder, statutory, and regulatory requirements. The role encompasses mentoring and supervising finance staff, ensuring robust financial systems and controls are in place, and providing high-quality financial insights to support effective programme delivery and organisational decision making.

Working closely the Chief Operations Officer (COO) the Head of Finance is responsible for embedding sound financial management across the organisation, ensuring stewardship, accountability, transparency and long-term financial sustainability.

Areas of Responsibilities

Financial Management and Reporting

  • Lead the preparation of accurate and timely financial reports, for budget holder, management, board, donors and other stakeholders.
  • Oversee organisational budgeting, forecasting and financial performance monitoring.
  • Ensure the timely preparation of annual financial statements and compliance with IFRS, US GAAP and other applicable standards.
  • Oversee month-end and year-end processes, including the review of balance sheet reconciliations and financial controls.
  • Lead and coordinate statutory, organisational, donor and project audits, ensuring compliance with regulatory and donor requirements.
  • Review and approve donor financial reports ensuring accuracy and compliance with the accounting system and funding agreements.
  • Oversee financial systems and reporting tools ensuring they effectively support financial management, reporting, compliance and decision making.
  • Drive continuous improvement in financial processes, controls and systems to enhance efficiency, accountability and data integrity.
  • Ensure compliance with tax, statutory and regulatory requirements across relevant jurisdictions.

Accounting, Control systems and procedures

  • Lead the design, implementation and continuous improvement of financial policies, procedures, controls and systems to ensure effective financial governance and accountability.
  • Maintain and periodically review the finance manual and related policies to ensure they remain fit for purpose and aligned with organisational needs, regulatory and donor requirements and best practice.
  • Ensure integrity, reliability and effectiveness of financial systems.
  • Drive innovation and digital transformation within the finance function by identifying and implementing system enhancements, automation opportunities, and best practice solutions that improve efficiency, data quality, and decision making.
  • Provide financial analysis, insights and recommendations to support decision making by Budget holders, management, and the board.
  • Monitor compliance with approved financial policies, procedures and internal controls across the organization and address areas of non-compliance.

Budgeting & Budgetary Control

  • Lead the development and consolidation of organisational budgets and forecast ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and available resources.
  • Oversee budget performance through regular monitoring and expenditure analysis against approved budget and recommending corrective actions.
  • Coordinate the preparation and review of proposal budgets ensuring cost recovery, compliance with donor requirements and alignment with organisational priorities.
  • Strengthen budgeting and financial management capacity across the organisation providing guidance, training and support to budget holders in the management of restricted and unrestricted funds.
  • Support budget holders to make informed financial decisions through the provision of budget analysis, forecasting and financial planning insights.

People Management

  • Supervise and mentor a high performing finance function, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement and a high standard of service.
  • Build team capacity through effective coaching, professional development and knowledge sharing.
  • Set clear objectives and conduct probation, performance and development reviews ensuring team performance aligns with organisation goals.
  • Support and empower team members to maximise their effectiveness, delivering high quality responsive and value-added service across the organisation.

Others

  • Undertake other duties and responsibilities, as reasonably required, that are consistent with the scope, seniority and objectivity of the role.
  • Provide high-quality ad hoc financial analysis, modelling, forecasts and scenario planning to support strategic decision-making, organisational planning and resource allocation.
  • Contribute to organisational initiatives, cross functional projects and change management activities providing financial expertise and leadership as required.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of the organisational priorities, risks and opportunities, proactively identifying and addressing emerging financial issues.
  • Act as a champion of sound financial stewardship, accountability and continuous improvement across the organisation.
  • Demonstrate and promote CIVICUS’ values and principles fostering a culture of collaboration, integrity, inclusion and respect.

Person Specification

Education and Language& Qualifications

  • A recognised professional qualified accountant (ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CIPFA or equivalent) with at least seven years post qualification experience, including at least 3 years in a Head of Finance role.
  • Senior level experience in a finance leadership role within an organisation of similar scale and complexity.
  • Strong written and verbal English skills.

Essential Knowledge, skills and Experience

  • Experience in the non-profit sector.
  • Extensive experience in establishing and administering financial processes for restricted donor funding within the not for profit sector.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of institutional donor regulations and financial compliance standards, including those of the European Union, US Foundations and European government agencies.
  • Ability to analyse, evaluate, and summarise financial records for accuracy and compliance with procedures, rules, and regulations, while effectively communicating financial information to non-financial team member in a clear and understandable manner.
  • Extensive experience in creating and leading training interventions for non-finance teams to enhance organisation financial management and adherence to financial standards.
  • Proven ability to build and lead high-performing, geographically dispersed teams by empowering employees, delegating responsibilities effectively, clearly defining roles, and promoting individual and team accountability.

Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience

  • Sound understanding ofhuman rights and social justice principles.
  • Proven experience in driving innovation through the implementation of automated financial systems, process improvements, and technology solutions to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and financial reporting.
  • Knowledge of one or more UN languages other than English is desirable.

The closing deadline for applications is on the 14th of August 2026 at 11:59pm SAST. Short listed candidates will be contacted 3 weeks after the closing date to schedule interviews.

Application instructions:

  • Applicants are advised not to use autofill when completing the application form for this job. To avoid errors, please fill out the form manually without using autofill.
  • AI-generated CVs/resumes and cover letters are not permitted. All application materials must be written by the applicant and accurately reflect the applicant’s skills, qualifications, and experience. Applications that contain AI-generated materials will not be considered.

We appreciate and consider each application submitted. However, given the large volume of applications received, we find it impossible to respond to each applicant immediately. You will hear from us within three weeks only if you’re shortlisted for the next steps. We will update all applicants once the position has been filled.

CIVICUS reserves the right to withdraw any of our vacancies at any time.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

You're the first voice prospects hear — and the first impression that sets the tone for every deal. As an inbound SDR at ShareGate, your job is to turn hand-raisers and signups into qualified conversations and hand them off to the AE team with everything they need to win. This role exists because we're growing, because we promote from within, and because we're looking for someone who wants to build a real B2B sales career with a team that actually invests in making them better.

Your impact:

  • Drive consistent, qualified pipeline for the AE team by converting inbound interest into SQL-ready opportunities — at a volume and quality that moves the needle on ARR;
  • Qualify every prospect with a consultative lens: understand their reality, challenge, and readiness before pushing forward, so every handoff lands with context, not just contact info;
  • Own your product knowledge across both ShareGate products (Protect and Migrate) and the IT personas we serve, so every conversation is grounded in real expertise rather than a generic pitch;
  • Embed AI tools into every part of your workflow — call prep, outreach, follow-ups, pipeline management — and treat them as a genuine performance accelerator, not a novelty;
  • Bring fresh ideas and new approaches to the team's process, especially around AI, contributing to a culture where everyone makes the whole team better.

Your team

You're joining a four-person inbound SDR team, all focused on ShareGate, feeding the AE org. That means the quality of what you pass downstream matters as much as the volume. The team is coached closely — Gong call reviews, roleplay sessions, custom AI tools, and a manager whose job is to help you grow. We move fast, share what's working, and hold each other to a high standard.

What you'll bring

  • An active daily user of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or equivalent) — not experimenting, actually using them to do better work, and ready to pick up new tools quickly;
  • Strong verbal communication in English — confident on the phone and on video, with a presence that creates a memorable first impression for the right reasons;
  • Experience in a sales or performance-driven role (SDR, BDR, inside sales) with a track record of hitting targets;
  • The ability to quickly learn complex products and understand the buyers who use them in a B2B context;
  • Pipeline discipline: you can prioritize, track, and advance multiple conversations in parallel without things slipping through;
  • Bonus: SaaS or tech background; familiarity with Gong, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, or HubSpot; ability to communicate in French.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary:$55k - $60k. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
    • OTE: $85k - $90k
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gathering twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

jobs.title: Consultancy - Conflict Sensitivity Assessment
jobs.excerpt: Overview & ResponsibilitiesBackgroundWith financial support from the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the International Development Law Organization (IDLO) will implement the Damal Programme Phase II – Strengthening the Social Contract through Access to Justice in Somaliland (2026–2030).
jobs.description:
Overview & Responsibilities

Background

With financial support from the Government of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the International Development Law Organization (IDLO) will implement the Damal Programme Phase II – Strengthening the Social Contract through Access to Justice in Somaliland (2026–2030). The programme seeks to strengthen the social contract in Somalia by improving the legitimacy, effectiveness, and inclusiveness of justice sector institutions at national, regional, and district levels. Building on the achievements of Damal Programme Phase I (2021–2026), Damal II will consolidate and expand access to justice interventions through three mutually reinforcing outcomes:

  • improved access to Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms and referral pathways, particularly for vulnerable groups;
  • enhanced access to formal justice through integrated support for survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) and other vulnerable justice seekers; and
  • increased citizen participation in accountability processes relating to justice and security.

The programme will commence with a preparatory phase designed to establish the strategic, operational, and analytical foundations for implementation. During this period, IDLO will undertake a series of complementary assessments, including a Baseline Assessment and Legal Analysis, Political Economy Analysis (PEA), Conflict Sensitivity Assessment (CSA), and Gender Analysis, to validate programme assumptions, refine implementation strategies, strengthen the Theory of Change, and ensure that programme interventions are evidence-based, conflict-sensitive, gender-responsive, and locally owned.

The Conflict Sensitivity Assessment will not start from a blank evidence base. It will build directly on the evidence, operational experience, and learning generated under Damal Programme Phase I. In particular, the consultant will review and use the 2021 Conflict Analysis, mid-term and end-of-Damal I evaluation reports, the 2021 Baseline Assessment and Legal Analysis, and the series of Political Economy Analyses conducted under Damal I. These documents will guide the consultant in understanding historical conflict dynamics, programme risks, institutional relationships, regional variations, and lessons learned from previous ADR, referral, legal aid, GBV response, and community justice interventions. The consultant will validate, update, and expand these findings to reflect the current context and the design priorities of Damal II.

Purpose and Objectives

The purpose of this assignment is to conduct a detailed Conflict Sensitivity Assessment that will help IDLO and its partners understand how conflict, fragility, social tensions, clan dynamics, displacement, political contestation, resource competition, insecurity, and local power relations may affect the design and implementation of Damal II.

The assessment will support IDLO to apply a “do no harm” approach and ensure that programme interventions are designed and implemented in ways that avoid reinforcing exclusion, mistrust, elite capture, clan bias, gender inequality, or local conflict. The specific objectives are to:

  • Analyse current and emerging conflict dynamics in Damal II target areas and assess their implications for justice and security programming.
  • Update and validate the findings of the 2021 Conflict Analysis identifying which conflict dynamics remain relevant, which have changed, and which new risks have emerged.
  • Identify conflict drivers, connectors, dividers, peace capacities, local power relations, institutional tensions, and community resilience mechanisms relevant to the three Damal II outcomes.
  • Assess how programme interventions may unintentionally exacerbate conflict, social divisions, local competition, mistrust, exclusion, or perceptions of bias.
  • Identify practical opportunities for Damal II to contribute positively to social cohesion, community trust, inclusive justice, peaceful dispute resolution, and accountable justice-security coordination.
  • Develop clear conflict risk mitigation measures for programme targeting partner selection, staffing, community engagement, referral systems, ADR support, institutional coordination, and communications.
  • Develop a simple and practical conflict monitoring tool that Damal II teams and partners can use throughout implementation to track conflict dynamics and adapt activities accordingly.
  • Provide recommendations on how to update the Risk Register included in the Damal II proposal package.

The Assignment

Under the overall supervision of the IDLO Damal II Field Programme Manager and in close collaboration with the Damal II Programme Team, the consultant will assess conflict sensitivity across Damal II’s target geographies and programme outcomes. The assessment will cover national, regional, district, and community-level conflict dynamics, with particular focus on rural, underserved, urban, and conflict-affected areas. The scope will include:

Conflict dynamics and context

  • Identify the main conflict drivers affecting the programme areas, including clan disputes, land and natural resource conflicts, political competition, displacement, revenge cycles, youth unemployment, gender-based violence, migration pressures, social exclusion, and tensions linked to justice and security institutions.
  • Analyse how conflict dynamics differ between regions, districts, urban centres, rural areas, IDP communities, minority communities, and border or disputed areas.
  • Assess how historical grievances, recent violence, local reconciliation efforts, and shifting political-security dynamics affect justice service delivery.
  • Identify conflict connectors, including shared institutions, community leaders, religious actors, women’s networks, youth platforms, ADR actors, legal aid providers, civil society organisations, and existing peacebuilding mechanisms.

Conflict sensitivity of ADR and reconciliation services

  • Assess how ADR and reconciliation services may interact with local conflict dynamics.
  • Identify risks of clan bias, elite capture, exclusion of women and minorities, harmful customary practices, informal fees, weak accountability, and inconsistent referral of cases beyond ADR mandates.
  • Examine whether ADR actors are viewed as legitimate, impartial, accessible, and trusted by different groups.
  • Identify how Damal II can strengthen ADR services without reinforcing harmful power structures or excluding vulnerable groups.

Conflict sensitivity of justice-security coordination

  • Assess how conflict and insecurity affect relationships between communities, police, prosecutors, courts, ADR actors, local authorities, and civil society.
  • Examine whether justice-security coordination platforms could create perceptions of securitisation, political alignment, exclusion, or bias.
  • Identify risks linked to information-sharing, case referrals, community policing, local security committees, and coordination with formal justice institutions.
  • Recommend ways to make justice-security coordination inclusive, accountable, transparent, and trusted by communities.

Conflict sensitivity of referral systems

  • Analyse conflict-related risks affecting referral pathways for cases beyond ADR mandates, including GBV, serious crimes, child protection cases, minority rights issues, land disputes, and cases involving IDPs.
  • Assess risks to survivors and vulnerable justice seekers, including retaliation, stigma, confidentiality breaches, pressure to reconcile, or forced settlement.
  • Identify practical safeguards to ensure that referral systems are safe, rights-based, gender-responsive, and conflict-sensitive.
  • Examine coordination between ADR actors, legal aid providers, police, courts, prosecutors, health services, psychosocial support providers, shelters, and community structures.

Programme-level conflict risks

  • Assess conflict risks related to geographic targeting, beneficiary selection, partner selection, cooperative agreements, recruitment, procurement, communications, training, grants, visibility, and resource distribution.
  • Identify stakeholders, institutions, relationships, or partnerships that may carry heightened conflict sensitivity risks.
  • Recommend mitigation measures for programme planning, implementation, monitoring, and adaptive management.
  • Provide practical guidance on how Damal II can avoid doing harm while maximising its contribution to social cohesion and trust-building.

Methodology

The Conflict Sensitivity Assessment will adopt a structured, participatory, conflict-sensitive, gender-responsive, and evidence-based methodology that combines desk research, institutional analysis, stakeholder consultations, and primary field research. The methodology will build on the extensive analytical work undertaken during Damal I, particularly the 2021 Conflict Analysis, ensuring that the assessment updates existing evidence rather than duplicating previous studies. The assessment will apply the principles of conflict sensitivity, Do No Harm, inclusion, and adaptive programming throughout the research process.

The methodology will address key research questions on conflict dynamics, access to justice, alternative dispute resolution (ADR), justice-security coordination, referral pathways, and programme adaptation. It will examine how conflict affects justice service delivery and provide practical recommendations to strengthen the design, implementation, monitoring, and adaptive management of Damal II. The consultant will triangulate evidence from multiple sources to ensure findings are robust, balanced, and grounded in the realities of the programme areas.

Please refer here to the detailed methodology.

Expected Final Report Structure

The final report should include:

  • Executive summary.
  • Background and purpose of the assessment.
  • Methodology, limitations, ethical considerations, and data sources.
  • Summary of findings from the 2021 Conflict Analysis and Damal I PEAs.
  • Updated conflict context analysis.
  • Regional, district, and community-level conflict dynamics.
  • Conflict actors, connectors, dividers, and peace capacities.
  • Conflict sensitivity analysis across the three Damal II outcomes.
  • Risks affecting vulnerable justice seekers.
  • Programme risk matrix and mitigation measures.
  • Recommendations for targeting, sequencing, partnerships, communications, training, referral systems, ADR support, and justice-security coordination.
  • Conflict monitoring tool for programme use.
  • Annexes, including tools, stakeholder list, documents reviewed, and anonymised data summaries.

Job Requirements

The consultant should have:

  • Advanced degree in conflict studies, peacebuilding, law, political science, governance, development studies, sociology, anthropology, or a related field.
  • At least 10 years of experience conducting conflict analysis, conflict sensitivity assessments, peacebuilding research, rule of law assessments, or governance analysis in fragile and conflict-affected contexts.
  • Strong knowledge of Somaliland and/or Somalia, including clan dynamics, customary justice, formal justice institutions, security actors, displacement, gender dynamics, and local conflict systems.
  • Demonstrated experience analysing the interaction between justice interventions and conflict dynamics.
  • Experience working on ADR, reconciliation, legal aid, GBV referral systems, justice-security coordination, community safety, and access to justice.
  • Strong understanding of do-no-harm principles, ethical research, safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection.
  • Excellent facilitation, stakeholder engagement, analytical writing, and communication skills.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Somali language skills are a strong asset.

Terms & Conditions

The consultancy will primarily be home-based, with travel to programme implementation areas and stakeholder locations as required to undertake field research, institutional consultations, and validation workshops. The consultant is expected to undertake missions to selected programme locations, subject to prevailing security conditions and operational requirements.

The consultancy period, level of effort, remuneration, and payment schedule will be specified in the consultancy contract. Payments will be linked to the satisfactory completion and approval of agreed deliverables in accordance with IDLO's contractual procedures.

All work produced under this assignment, including reports, datasets, interview records, analytical tools, presentations, and supporting documentation, shall become the property of IDLO. The consultant shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all information obtained during the assignment and comply with IDLO's policies on research ethics, data protection, safeguarding, and information security.

IDLO is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for IDLO vacancies.

IDLO does not tolerate sexual exploitation or abuse, any kind of harassment, including harassment of a sexual nature, or discrimination. As such, IDLO will conduct careful reference and background checks of all selected candidates as part of its selection process.

Application deadline: 23 August 2026 (23:59hrs Rome Time).

Vir Biotechnology has exclusive rights to the universal PRO-XTEN® masking platform for oncology and infectious disease. PRO-XTEN® is a trademark of Amunix Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a Sanofi company.

We believe the success of our colleagues drives the success of our mission. We are committed to creating a company where everyone feels supported and encouraged to give their best.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Vice President, Business Development Transactions (Temporary) will serve as the Company's senior transaction lead for strategic partnering activities, with primary responsibility for structuring, negotiating, and executing complex business development transactions involving the Company's oncology portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Business Officer, this individual will provide expert transactional leadership across the full deal lifecycle, including confidentiality agreements, term sheets, diligence processes, definitive agreements, and post-signing governance support.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Research, Development, Commercial, Finance, Legal, Intellectual Property, Alliance Management, and Executive Leadership teams to maximize the value of the Company's clinical-stage and preclinical oncology assets through regional and global licensing, co-development, co-commercialization, collaboration, option, and platform transactions.

This role requires exceptional deal judgment, strong negotiation skills, deep understanding of biopharmaceutical transaction structures, and the ability to drive negotiations with senior executives and external counsel representing global biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies.

Transaction Leadership

  • Lead, or support the CBO in leading, the negotiation and execution of strategic partnering transactions involving oncology therapeutics, technology platforms, and related intellectual property.
  • Serve as one of the Company's principal negotiators for non-binding term sheets, letters of intent, option agreements, collaboration agreements, license agreements, co-development agreements, and other strategic transactions.
  • Develop transaction structures and economic frameworks that maximize asset value while aligning with corporate objectives.
  • Identify key business, legal, regulatory, intellectual property, financial, and operational risks and develop strategies to mitigate such risks during negotiations.
  • Drive transactions from initial engagement through signing and closing, coordinating all internal stakeholders.

Deal Strategy and Structuring

  • Advise senior management regarding optimal transaction structures, including:
  • Global and regional licensing arrangements
  • Co-development and co-commercialization partnerships
  • Platform and technology licensing transactions
  • Research collaborations
  • Option-to-license structures
  • Asset acquisitions and divestitures

Negotiation and Contracting

  • Work closely with internal and external legal counsel to negotiate definitive agreements.
  • Ensure alignment between business objectives and contractual provisions.
  • Maintain consistency in transaction precedents, templates, and negotiation playbooks.

Portfolio and Business Development Support

  • Support evaluation of partnering opportunities for oncology programs and technology platforms.
  • Contribute to business case development and valuation analyses.
  • Provide transactional expertise during partner outreach, management presentations, and negotiations.

WHO YOU ARE AND WHAT YOU BRING

Required

  • Advanced degree in life sciences, business, law, or a related discipline (PhD, MD, MBA, JD, or equivalent preferred).
  • 12+ years of biotechnology, pharmaceutical, business development, legal, investment banking, consulting, or related experience.
  • Significant experience negotiating and executing biopharmaceutical licensing and collaboration transactions.

  • Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred

  • Experience with both preclinical and clinical-stage assets.
  • Prior experience negotiating transactions with large pharmaceutical companies.
  • Familiarity with global partnering structures, including ex-U.S. regional licensing arrangements.

Position Overview

The Director of Operational Accounting will serve as the executive leader responsible for the strategy, execution, and continuous optimization of Oura’s end-to-end transactional accounting functions: Accounts Payable (AP) Operations, Time & Expense (T&E), Payroll Operations, and Order to Cash Operations

In this role, you will build a high-performing team, drive global automation, establish robust internal controls, and lead cross-functional transformation across ERPs, HR systems, customer support platforms (Zendesk), and revenue operations.

Key Responsibilities

1. Accounts Payable Leadership

  • P2P Strategy & Team Execution: Partner with the Head of Procurement and own the global disbursements process, directing an AP team responsible for high-volume invoice processing, vendor onboarding, 1099/1042 compliance, and operational execution.
  • Spend Management & Automation: Spearhead the continuous optimization of P2P platforms (e.g., Coupa, Ramp, NetSuite) to drive strict 3-way matching, purchase order enforcement, and automated approval workflows across the enterprise.

  • AP Close & Compliance Accountability: Deliver a flawless month-end AP close, ensuring complete accuracy across unvouchered PO accruals, corporate card reconciliations, vendor statement audits, and dispute resolutions.
  • Team & Platform Ownership: Steering team operations and vendor management across enterprise T&E systems (e.g., Concur, Ramp, Navan) and card programs, optimizing integration architecture with ERPs like NetSuite, SAP, or Workday.

2. Payroll Operations & Human Capital Strategy

  • Global Payroll Delivery: Own the accurate, compliant, and timely execution of multi-state US and international payroll, statutory tax reporting, and regulatory compliance, leading a dedicated payroll team.
  • Cross-Functional HR & Equity Alignment: Drive alignment with HR Operations, Compensation, and Equity leadership to ensure seamless integration and accurate execution of stock-based compensation, benefits, mobility, and bonus structures.

  • Payroll Governance & Audit Readiness: Ensure strict compliance for all payroll journal entries, month-end reconciliations, tax filings (W-2s/W-8s), and internal payroll controls.

3. Order-to-Cash (O2C), Accounts Receivable & Billing

  • Multi-Channel O2C Ownership: Lead and hold ultimate accountability for the AR and Billing team managing complex, high-volume transactions across D2C e-commerce, subscription memberships, B2B enterprise sales, and retail channels.
  • Metrics & Balance Sheet Ownership: Directly own the operational execution and accuracy of Unbilled Receivables, Consolidated AR Aging, customer deposits, and credit/dunning policies.
  • Processor & Retail Reconciliation Governance: Drive the strategic oversight of payment gateway settlements (Stripe, Adyen), retail remittances (Best Buy, Target, Amazon), and payment recovery protocols to minimize friction and bad debt.
  • Cross - Accounting Partnership: Partner closely with Revenue Accounting and broader Accounting leadership to build strong operating connectivity across Accounting and ensure O2C processes, customer billing flows, credits, reserves, disputes, and cash application activities are operationally sound, aligned with revenue recognition policies, supportive of an accurate and efficient month-end close, and proactively resolved before issues impact reporting.
  • Cross-Functional & Upstream Integration: Champion deep cross-functional alignment between the O2C team, RevOps, Commercial Finance, and Member Experience (Zendesk) to eliminate upstream bottlenecks, dispute spikes, and refund delays.

4. Process Excellence, Governance & Systems Transformation

  • Operational Tech Roadmap: Act as the executive owner for finance operational technology, driving system implementations, upgrades, and integrations across ERPs, billing engines, payment gateways, and spend tools.
  • SOX Readiness & Control Environment: Establish, enforce, and maintain a robust internal control framework (SOX-readiness) across all AP, Payroll, and O2C workflows, guaranteeing proper segregation of duties and risk mitigation.
  • Audit Ownership & Deliverables:Own the operational month-end close timeline and serve as the primary accountable leader for external audit deliverables (PBCs), process narrative accuracy, and compliance sign-offs.
  • Operational Performance & KPI Delivery: Define and report key executive performance metrics (e.g., AP cycle time, payroll accuracy, DSO, unbilled balances, processor success rates) directly to senior finance leadership.
  • Outsourced Operations Governance: Design, implement, and enforce global operational frameworks and SLAs for third-party vendors and outsourced teams—ensuring high delivery quality, regulatory compliance, and cost efficiency across all external engagements.

Qualifications

  • Education & Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business; CPA, CMA, or MBA strongly preferred.
  • Industry Background: Strong experience in fast-growing D2C e-commerce, consumer hardware, retail distribution, or SaaS/subscription-based environments.
  • Technical Expertise: Advanced proficiency with modern ERPs (e.g., NetSuite, Workday), billing engines (e.g., Stripe, Zuora, Recurly), spend management tools (e.g., Zip, Ramp), payroll systems (e.g., ADP, Workday Payroll), and customer service platforms (Zendesk).

Recognized by TIME as one of the Top 10 Most Influential Software Companies of 2026 and by Inc. for Best in Business for Innovation, Pindrop is backed by leading investors including Andreessen Horowitz, IVP, and CapitalG.

What you'll do

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Authentication team, you will help build and scale the cloud services behind Passport as the team continues moving customers onto its cloud platform. You’ll focus on highly reliable, secure authentication services that power voice-based identity verification at scale, while increasingly leveraging AI/ML-driven signals and tooling to strengthen fraud defenses and engineering productivity. More specifically, you will:

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and monitor high-performance backend services and APIs using Go and Python, with an emphasis on secure, low-latency authentication and identity workflows.
  • Build and maintain cloud‑native services across AWS and GCP (e.g., S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, IAM) with a focus on reliability, scale, and secure production operation, including data pipelines that feed downstream ML and risk models used in authentication decisions.
  • Deliver features and enhancements through the full software development lifecycle, including implementation, automated testing, deployment, and operational support, using CI/CD and infrastructure‑as‑code practices.
  • Tackle complex software engineering problems in authentication, identity, and fraud prevention—contributing to architecture decisions, threat‑aware design, and continuous improvement of engineering best practices across the team.
  • Integrate and consume AI/ML capabilities (for example, model-backed risk scores, deepfake detection signals, or ML‑driven policies) by collaborating with Research, MLOps, and Protect/Passport teams, and help productionize these models into scalable, observable services.
  • Use observability and diagnostics tooling (metrics, logging, tracing, dashboards) to troubleshoot production issues, reduce alert noise, and systematically improve reliability and latency for authentication journeys.
  • Partner closely with software engineering, test engineering, research, product, Protect, Passport, and Core teams to deliver new capabilities and improve existing ones, including AI‑enhanced identity and fraud experiences for customers.
  • Participate in the team’s on‑call rotation, including helping cover after‑hours alerts as we expand distributed support coverage for our customer‑facing authentication platform.
  • Contribute to documentation, runbooks, and design reviews that clarify how authentication services behave, how AI/ML components are used safely, and how other engineers should integrate with the platform.

Who you are

  • You are a strong communicator who collaborates effectively across engineering, product, test, research, and other cross‑functional partners.
  • You are an owner who can independently drive work from design through production with strong judgment around performance, scale, security, and reliability in authentication flows.
  • You are energized by solving hard technical problems and improving systems, processes, and engineering standards, especially in high‑stakes, security‑sensitive environments.
  • You are resilient, adaptable, and effective in environments that require context switching, rapid troubleshooting, and operating through ambiguity while maintaining high quality.
  • You are resourceful and curious—comfortable learning new tools (including AI tooling) and teaching yourself what you need to move a problem forward, then sharing that knowledge with the team.
  • You are invested in helping others grow and bring a mentorship mindset to code reviews, pairing, and day‑to‑day collaboration.

Your skill-set

Must-haves:

  • 5-7+ years of professional software development experience building backend services and APIs.
  • Strong experience with Go, Python, or similar languages, plus a solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and Linux-based development.
  • Hands-on experience designing and operating cloud-native systems in AWS or GCP, including managed services such as S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, and IAM.
  • Experience with CI/CD, DevOps, Docker, Kubernetes, and production ownership, including deploying, monitoring, troubleshooting, and supporting services in live environments.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with backend data stores and messaging technologies such as Redis, MySQL, RabbitMQ, and Elasticsearch.
  • Experience in authentication, identity, fraud prevention, or other security-sensitive product environments.
  • Experience with observability tooling and production diagnostics across metrics, logging, and tracing.
  • Exposure to UI work or adjacent product experiences that connect backend systems to customer-facing workflows.

What's in it for you

At Pindrop, you’ll work on the backend and platform systems that power Passport, helping secure critical customer interactions where trust, fraud prevention, and identity verification matter every day. You’ll tackle meaningful cloud engineering challenges that shape reliability, scalability, and the speed at which products reach customers, with direct visibility into the impact of your work. As a senior engineer, you’ll have the opportunity to influence architecture, raise technical standards, and help strengthen a growing team alongside experienced partners across the platform. You’ll join a company operating at the intersection of authentication, fraud prevention, and deepfake defense, where strong engineering directly supports the business and the customers who rely on it.

What we offer

As a part of Pindrop, you’ll have a direct impact on our growing list of products and the future of security in the voice-driven economy. We hire great people and take care of them. Here’s a snapshot of the benefits we offer:

  • Competitive compensation package, including RSUs (Restricted Stock Units) for all employees, so everyone shares in our long-term success.
  • Remote-first environment - giving you flexibility and autonomy in how you structure your day.
  • While we work flexibly, we prioritize meaningful in-person moments through regular team on-sites, company-wide events, and intentional gatherings that foster connection, collaboration, and shared success.
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Generous health and welfare plans to choose from - including one employer-paid “employee-only” plan!
  • Best-in-class Health Savings Account (HSA) employer contribution
  • Low-cost vision and dental plans for you and your family, providing comprehensive coverage and peace of mind.
  • Paid Parental Leave - Including birth, adoptive & foster parents
    • One year of diaper delivery for your newest addition to the family! It’s our way of welcoming new Pindroplets to the family!
  • Recurring monthly phone and internet allowance to help cover essential connectivity costs and support flexible work.
  • Enhanced fertility and GLP-1 benefits to support family-building journeys and personalized health needs.
  • Annual Learning & Development stipend to support your professional growth, skill-building, certifications, and continued education.

Please note that the base pay range is a general guideline only. Pindrop considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, a candidate's work experience, education/training, and key skills, as well as market and business considerations, when extending an offer.

US Base Pay Range
$130,000—$170,000 USD

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team, with a broad range of experience and perspectives. If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, apply anyway! We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

AI - A Transformative Force

At Pindrop, we view artificial intelligence as a transformative force that, when harnessed responsibly, can unlock unprecedented value for our customers, partners and society and enable and empower us to continue to deliver cutting-edge technology to combat fraud and unblur the lines between what it means to be human versus machine.

Applications with the strongest match to job requirements are prioritized for human review; not all applications may be individually reviewed.

About Airship

Airship is trusted by world’s leading brands such as Alaska Airlines, BBC and The Home Depot to drive revenue growth and customer loyalty with exceptional cross-channel customer experiences. Today, brands are challenged to deliver seamless, unified customer experiences across a fragmented array of channels and devices— apps, websites, email, SMS, wallets and more.

We invite you to be part of our journey in building products and delivering services that touch millions of customers around the world every day.

To learn more about us, visit , read our blog or follow us on LinkedIn.

About Gummicube

Gummicube is a specialized division within Airship Group, Inc., focused exclusively on app discovery, App Store Optimization, mobile growth, and app store conversion. Gummicube helps brands grow high-quality mobile app audiences by improving visibility and conversion across the App Store and Google Play. Our work combines proprietary technology with hands-on strategy, analytics, creative testing, and client services. Gummicube serves apps of every size and category, including enterprise brands, high-growth startups, and new app launches.

Although Gummicube is part of Airship Group, this is a Gummicube-specific role. Candidates hired into this position will work with Gummicube's team, clients, services, and proprietary ASO technologies.
Gummicube's culture is entrepreneurial, collaborative, client-focused, and hands-on. We value people who are curious about mobile growth, comfortable working across functions, and motivated by helping customers improve performance through data-driven recommendations and disciplined execution.

For more information, visit

About the Role

At Gummicube, you will work in a focused, specialized business where app store performance, mobile growth, client outcomes, and data-driven execution are central to the work. Our teams are intentionally cross-functional, which means you'll often see how your work affects the full ASO process, including strategy, analytics, creative, client delivery, and product feedback. This is a good fit for someone who enjoys agency-style client work, fast-moving priorities, practical problem solving, and close collaboration with teammates across disciplines.

In this role, you will lead growth strategy and revenue expansion across a portfolio of ASO and mobile growth clients. You'll combine performance marketing expertise with consultative leadership to help clients achieve measurable results.

What You'll Do

  • Own client growth, retention, and revenue expansion for a portfolio of Gummicube accounts, using strategic planning and data-driven recommendations to deliver measurable business outcomes
  • Lead business reviews, quarterly planning sessions, and growth strategy presentations for your clients, translating complex performance data into clear, actionable recommendations
  • Mentor and develop Growth Managers, Analysts, and Specialists on your team, providing strategic guidance and career development support
  • Drive budget expansion and secure incremental investment opportunities by demonstrating value through forecasting, scenario planning, and financial modeling
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives across Paid Media, Business Development, and Account teams to align client strategy with Gummicube's ASO methodology and services
  • Improve operational excellence by developing processes, documentation, and best practices that raise the bar for the broader team
  • Use attribution platforms, analytics tools, and data visualization solutions to inform strategy and drive business decisions
  • Use AI-powered tools where appropriate to improve personal productivity, reporting efficiency, and strategic analysis

*Duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands. Responsibilities may be amended at any time at the sole discretion of the Employer.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in growth marketing, performance marketing, user acquisition, digital marketing, or a related field
  • 2–3 years of experience leading client strategy, owning accounts, and managing teams
  • Experience managing $1M+ in annual media budget (or equivalent portfolio responsibility)
  • Track record of growing revenue, client spend, or portfolio value
  • Experience presenting performance results and strategy recommendations to executive stakeholders
  • Deep familiarity with digital marketing metrics: CAC, ROAS, LTV, retention, incrementality, and attribution
  • Direct experience building campaigns on platforms such as Apple Search Ads, Meta (Facebook/Instagram), Google App Campaigns, or similar
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adjust your style based on your audience
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, client-focused, remote environment
  • Strong ownership, follow-through, and attention to detail

We'd Be Delighted If You Also Have

  • Experience with App Store Optimization, app store analytics, or mobile conversion optimization
  • Experience working with enterprise clients or in agency-style client engagements
  • Familiarity with Gummicube's tools, the App Store, Google Play, or app store creative testing and conversion optimization
  • Experience analyzing complex issues and developing realistic plans, programs, and recommendations for diverse stakeholders
  • Comfort presenting to C-level stakeholders and connecting marketing activities to broader business objectives
  • Experience experimenting with AI tools in your personal or professional life - or an eagerness to learn

Work Location & Travel Requirements

Airship’s ‘Digital First’ approach to work means that for the majority of our roles, work can be performed remotely, either some or most of the time. Airship believes that flexible work contributes to a more productive and more equitable work environment, and that Airshippers are able to collaborate, innovate, and support one another across different locations and timezones.

Some roles may require that employees perform their work from a specific location to support business activities, and/or be within proximity to an Airship office location or customer or partner locations, while other roles can be performed 100% remotely.

This position is fully remote and may require up to 10% travel based on business needs or as requested by your manager.

Compensation

Starting Pay Range: $130,000-$145,000 USD per year

This is a good faith estimate of the base compensation we reasonably expect to pay for this position upon hire. Actual starting pay may vary based on factors such as relevant skills, work experience, market demands, and location. All offers include stock options so employees have the opportunity to benefit from Airship’s success.

Benefits & Perks

  • Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance options for you and your dependents
  • Flexible time off, company paid holidays, paid parental leave, and paid volunteer time off
  • Support for your overall wellbeing with mental health and wellness resources
  • Employer-subsidized life insurance as well as short-term and long-term disability
  • A digital-first work environment and a monthly stipend to support remote work
  • Mentorship and growth opportunities to build skills and accelerate professional development
  • And more!

We use artificial intelligence tools in our recruitment process as decision-support tools only. Airship's People Operations team reviews all AI-generated scores and recommendations before making any hiring determination. No applicant is rejected solely on the basis of an AI-generated output. Depending on your location, you may have the right to request human review of any AI-assisted employment decision or to opt out of AI evaluation. Hiring Commitment

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

The role is part of the IT Function within the broader Mozilla Infrastructure team. The IT team supports ERP Services, Workplace services, Service-Desk and On-Prem DC Services across the organization aligned with the mission to build a safe & secure internet. As a Software (Application) Engineer in the newly formed Workplace technology team, you’ll help design, build, and maintain the systems and automations that power Mozilla’s workplace technologies — from collaboration and AI productivity tools to identity and access workflows. You’ll manage day-to-day administration, develop scripts and integrations, and contribute to projects that improve reliability, security, and user experience. This role is hands-on and growth-oriented, offering opportunities to deepen your technical expertise while shaping how Mozillians work and collaborate.

Note: You don’t need to meet every listed qualification to be considered — we value diverse experiences and learning potential.

What you’ll do:

  • Design, build, and maintain scripts, APIs, and workflow automations that power key workplace systems — collaboration tools (Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Atlassian) and identity platforms (Okta).
  • Develop lightweight services or integrations that connect collaboration, GenAI-tools (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) and internal systems, enabling agentic flows (e.g., virtual assistants, workflow agents) that reduce manual work and improve user experience.
  • Implement monitoring, logging and observability for automation and AI workflows; troubleshoot issues and uncover opportunities for reliability, scalability, and cost-efficiency.
  • Contribute to the evolution of secure onboarding, off-boarding, and mover workflows across access, permissions and SaaS tools — with automation and safe agentic handoffs where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with IT, Security, and People teams to ensure identity, data, and compliance standards (SSO, DLP, classification) are deeply embedded through automation and script-driven guardrails.
  • Participate in pilot projects for new AI and productivity capabilities: integrate LLMs & agents, track usage/adoption metrics, build flows that assist users (e.g., knowledge-agent, document summarizer).
  • Contribute to the code-review process, documentation of shared libraries for workflows/agents, and build a library of integration templates for reuse across the team.
  • Partner with senior engineers to modernize workplace systems through scalable architecture, API-first design, and intelligent agentic workflows.

What you'll bring:

  • 4–6 years of experience in software engineering, systems integration or workplace technology development, with a focus on automation or scripting.

Organizational Mission:

The Appalachian Trail Conservancy’s mission is to protect, manage, and advocate for the Appalachian National Scenic Trail.

Position Summary

The Landscape Conservation Program Director reports to the Vice President, Conservation and Government Relations and provides strategic leadership for ATC's landscape conservation portfolio, aligning partners, investments, and conservation action to advance a conserved and connected Appalachian Trail landscape. The Director establishes program direction, mobilizes collaborative conservation efforts across multiple scales, and positions ATC as a trusted leader in landscape-scale conservation.

The Director oversees the Appalachian Trail Landscape Partnership, regional and place-based partnerships, the A.T. Communities Program, the Wild East Action Fund, and conservation decision-support initiatives. Working across departments and with external partners, the Director translates strategy into measurable conservation, partnership, funding, and policy outcomes.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Strategy

  • Establish and continually refine ATC's landscape conservation strategy and long-term vision.
  • Align staff, work plans, partnerships, and investments with organizational priorities.
  • Represent ATC's landscape conservation vision with leadership, the Board, partners, agencies, and funders.
  • Build organizational capacity and sustainable funding.

Partnerships

  • Lead ATC's engagement in landscape-scale, regional, and place-based partnerships.
  • Align partners around shared priorities and collaborative initiatives.
  • Provide strategic leadership for the A.T. Communities Program as a gateway community recognition and grassroots engagement network.
  • Cultivate partnerships that reinforce ATC's role as a trusted convener and driver of meaningful impact.

Investment & Prioritization

  • Direct strategic deployment of the Wild East Action Fund and related conservation investments.
  • Guide prioritization of high-value conservation opportunities using science, GIS, and partner knowledge.
  • Promote practical decision-support tools.
  • Advance innovation through research partnerships.

Leadership & Accountability

  • Supervise staff and establish outcome-focused performance measures.
  • Monitor performance and adapt strategies using data and partner feedback.
  • Communicate accomplishments to leadership, funders, and the Board.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in environmental science, conservation, natural resource management, public administration, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 5-7 years of experience managing collaborative conservation, land protection, or landscape-scale conservation initiatives.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience leading staff, teams, programs, or significant crossfunctional initiatives, with demonstrated ability to establish priorities, develop organizational capacity, and drive accountability for results.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of landscape-scale conservation principles, land protection strategies, partnership development, and collaborative conservation approaches involving public, private, nonprofit, and community stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to provide strategic leadership across complex, multi-partner initiatives by influencing without direct authority, navigating competing interests, establishing shared priorities, and aligning diverse organizations and stakeholders to achieve measurable conservation outcomes.
  • Experience managing and developing grants, funding agreements, or conservation incentive programs, including tracking deliverables and compliance requirements.
  • Strong leadership presence and exceptional written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to communicate complex information, influence decision-making, and represent the organization effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and database systems, with the ability to effectively use data, technology, and performance measures to support program management and organizational decision-making.

Preferred Qualifications Experience

  • Experience with grant writing, grant administration, regranting programs, grant reporting, and conservation finance.
  • Knowledge of public and private conservation funding sources, including federal, state, philanthropic, and foundation grants.
  • Experience working with large-scale conservation partnerships, land trusts, government agencies, and regional conservation coalitions.
  • Experience engaging in rural communities and municipalities, particularly within the Appalachian region.
  • Three or more years of experience supervising staff, interns, volunteers, or project teams.
  • Proficiency with ESRI GIS applications and related data management and communication tools.
  • Familiarity with the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and its cooperative management framework.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

  • Ability to maintain a home office with reliable internet access; access to an ATC office may be available based on location and office capacity.
  • Ability to communicate effectively through virtual platforms, email, telephone, and in-person meetings.
  • Prolonged periods of computer and telephone use.
  • Periodic travel throughout ATC's 14-state service area and beyond for meetings, workshops, community events, and conferences (approximately 10–15% travel).
  • Occasional evening and weekend work required to support meetings, events, and partner engagement activities.

Additional Details:

  • Location: Residence in one of the 14 Trail states (Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Vermont, New Hampshire, and Maine).

Colorado Christian University cultivates knowledge and love of God in a Christ-centered community of learners and scholars, with an enduring commitment to the integration of exemplary academics, spiritual formation, and engagement with the world. We envision graduates who think critically and creatively, lead with high ethical and professional standards, embody the character and compassion of Jesus Christ, treasure the gospel, and who thereby are prepared to impact the world in their callings.

CCU embraces an educational model that was present at the foundation of many of the great western and American universities. It is made up of three pillars—competence, character and Christ-centered faith. Secular universities have abandoned two of those pillars. We think this is a major oversight that eventually undermines education. Furthermore, we believe this classical educational model is both life-giving and greatly needed in our time.

A leader in higher education, CCU has been consistently ranked in the top 2 percent of colleges and universities nationwide for its core curriculum by the American Council of Trustees and Alumni. CCU has had ten consecutive years of enrollment growth and has been named one of the five fastest-growing master’s granting universities by The Chronicle of Higher Education.

CCU offers more than 200 degree program options for traditional and adult students through its two colleges--the College of Undergraduate Studies and College of Adult and Graduate Studies. More than 8,000 students attend the University on the main campus, in regional centers throughout Colorado, and online.

What is most appealing about working at CCU?

  1. Faith-friendly: CCU’s culture is unique to higher education. Where else can you pursue academic excellence yet read the Holy Bible, pray with teammates and students at work, and work to impact our culture in support of Christian values?
  2. Convictionally Christian: As a university, we have an enduring commitment to Christ, his kingdom and the truth of God’s Word.
  3. Live out your calling: We are a traditional evangelical university where you can invest your God-given talents and abilities alongside coworkers and teammates, while having a profound influence on students as they deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ.
  4. Equip students for kingdom work: You can be a part of helping students discover their callings and preparing them for positions of significant leadership in the church, business, government, education, and other professions, as a key part of our University's Strategic Priorities.

We're looking for candidates who have:

  1. Bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university, Master's degree preferred. Professionals with education and/or experience commensurate with the duties described will also be considered.
  2. Two or more years of service as an academic advisor strongly preferred.
  3. Effective oral, interpersonal, and written communication skills. Exceptional customer service, problem solving, decision making, and creative thinking skills in a fast-paced environment are greatly desired.
  4. Self-confidence, patience, empathy, and availability when building rapport with constituents. Understands and adapts quickly to multi-generational needs and characteristics.
  5. Creative, out-of-the-box ideas and takes initiative to find solutions while clarifying and enforcing CCU’s expectations and policies.
  6. Flexibility, adaptive to change, and teachable; ability to actively locate appropriate resources to assist with unfamiliar situations, is comfortable asking questions, and recognizes and learns from mistakes.
  7. Ability to maintain cohesive working relationships, views conflict positively, and operates with honesty and respect in all communication.
  8. Familiarity with adult education and academic environment.
  9. High technology proficiency including Microsoft products.
  10. Bilingual speaking and writing proficiency in Spanish/English preferred.

Key Job Duties

Horace Mann is seeking an experienced and technically skilled Large Loss Adjuster to manage high-exposure homeowner property claims, including complex and litigated files. The ideal candidate thrives in complex claim environments, demonstrates strong business acumen, and brings deep knowledge of policy interpretation, dwelling estimating, and litigation management.

Complex Claims Handling

  • Manage and investigate large loss and high-exposure homeowner claims, including litigation files and claims involving public adjusters and attorneys.
  • Verify coverage, interpret policy language, and determine liability and scope of damages.
  • Evaluate claim facts and damage estimates to move claims toward appropriate and timely resolution.
  • Apply in-depth knowledge of homeowner's policies and jurisdictional documents to assigned claims.

Investigation & Damage Assessment

  • Conduct on-site inspections as needed to evaluate damages and determine loss exposure.
  • Investigate origin and cause of high-exposure claims, coordinating with insureds, claimants, agents, attorneys, contractors, experts, Special Investigation Unit (SIU), public officials, and other adjusters.
  • Identify prior losses and recognize potential environmental exposures.
  • Reconcile contractor and mitigation estimates and collaborate with vendors to determine appropriate damage valuations.
  • Demonstrate advanced proficiency in Xactimate, including preparation of large loss and total loss estimates (Level 3 certification encouraged).

Negotiation & Resolution

  • Negotiate settlements with insureds, attorneys, and public adjusters in accordance with company best practices.
  • Manage period of restoration for ALE (Additional Living Expense) and Loss of Rent claims.
  • Interpret and apply policies, leases, by-laws, declarations, and contract coverages as they apply to all parties involved.
  • Maintain transparent and timely communication with all stakeholders throughout the claim lifecycle.

Catastrophe & Collaboration

  • Provide assistance during catastrophe events as needed.
  • Participate in special projects and consult on process improvement initiatives.
  • Actively engage in mentoring and training of other claims professionals.

Qualifications & Experience

  • 5–7 years of dwelling estimating experience preferred, with demonstrated sustained technical performance.
  • Proven experience handling homeowner property losses of $50,000 or greater.
  • Strong claims and business acumen with litigation experience.
  • Advanced knowledge of homeowner policy interpretation and coverage analysis.
  • Demonstrated Xactimate expertise; encouraged to pursue Level 3 certification.
  • Ability to work effectively with vendors regarding damage determination and estimate reconciliation.
  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment using claims systems and telephony platforms.
  • Maintain and obtain required state adjuster licenses; ability to comply with all jurisdictional regulatory requirements.
